key_insight: Hierarchical randomized neural networks combine targeted initialization, deflated optimization, and multilevel refinement to find multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations efficiently and accurately.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help computational engineers identify distinct solution branches without prior knowledge of the solutions.
method: Use an SVD of a characteristic matrix built from network basis functions and sampling points to generate effective initial candidates.
Apply good deflated Gauss–Newton optimization with exponential deflation to search for distinct solutions.
Refine through hierarchical network levels to accelerate computation and improve accuracy.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests report relative errors reaching 10^-16, preservation of solution symmetries, and, in the best case, less than one-tenth of the comparison computational cost.
watch_item: The reported numerical results do not guarantee finding every solution, and the local error estimate requires additional conditions.
paper_title: Hierarchical randomized neural networks for efficiently and accurately finding multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
